extracted.intended_audience: EPA communications staff, press officers, and federal agency public affairs professionals who draft press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for drafting EPA press releases that are accurate, accessible, and compliant with agency and federal requirements. Covers tone, structure, style, scientific/contextual content, legal obligations, and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third person tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases written in third person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use third-person voice throughout the release; avoid using first person 'we' or 'I' in the body of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty / No spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty is the primary constituent and quality of all EPA communications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent and factual; avoid spin or misleading emphasis. Present limitations and uncertainty rather than overstating findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative but not propagandistic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey expertise and credibility without using promotional language or advocacy phrasing that could be perceived as propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-appropriate tone and content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor language, detail level, and emphasis to the intended audience identified in the release (general public, stakeholders, media, scientific community).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph length
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead Paragraph - Limited to 25 words or fewer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the lead concise (≤25 words). The lead should be short and immediately convey the main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead answers the 5Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell briefly: who, what, where, when, why
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the lead (first paragraph) answers who, what, where, when, and why about the event, issue, or project.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph includes main message
rubrics_metrics.description: First Paragraph Requirements - Main message included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the main message or key takeaway up front so readers understand the purpose immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear purpose statement in lead
rubrics_metrics.description: First Paragraph Requirements - Clear purpose statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the release's purpose in the lead (e.g., announce action, share findings, warn affected populations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience identified in lead
rubrics_metrics.description: First Paragraph Requirements - Intended audience identified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify who the release is for (e.g., residents of X county, stakeholders, press) so tone and content align with audience needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style adherence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow The Associated Press Stylebook for grammar, punctuation, capitalization, and common usage. Use Webster's Dictionary (first spelling preferred) for spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer active constructions to passive ones to make sentences clearer and more direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language for general audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in plain language appropriate for a general audience (implicit target: roughly Grade 8 reading level). Also comply with the Plain Writing Act of 2010.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all technical statements are accurate and vetted by subject-matter experts; avoid oversimplifying to the point of inaccuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific numbers and data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete figures, measurements, dates, and quantities rather than vague descriptors when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute facts, data, and quotes to credible sources; cite peer-reviewed literature where available and identify data sources clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide scientific context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how findings or actions fit into the broader scientific understanding; summarize relevant evidence without jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include data on affected populations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who is affected (demographics, numbers) and quantify impacts when possible to make the implications clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify geographic scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the geographic area to which the release applies (e.g., neighborhood, county, watershed, nationwide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed sources where available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scientific studies inform the release, cite peer-reviewed publications and provide appropriate context for their relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limits of knowledge, confidence intervals, or areas where more research is needed; avoid portraying uncertainty as ignorance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid alarmism without basis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sensationalize risks; present risk in proportion to evidence and provide context to avoid unnecessary panic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide actionable information for affected populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide actionable information for affected populations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, practical steps individuals or communities should take (e.g., boil water advisory instructions, contact numbers, evacuation guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include resources for more information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List websites, hotlines, guidance documents, or contact information where readers can learn more or get assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Writing Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release complies with the Plain Writing Act requirements for clarity and usability of federal communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make releases accessible per Section 508 requirements (e.g., accessible PDFs, alternative text, readable formatting) so people with disabilities can access the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA compliance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare releases mindful of Freedom of Information Act considerations (proper records handling, no improper withholding of required records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with affected stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate messaging with parties affected by the release (local officials, partner agencies, tribes, stakeholders) before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval through proper channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain necessary internal approvals (legal, program, communications leadership) prior to issuing the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Webster's spelling consistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Webster's Dictionary as the spelling authority and prefer the first listed spelling for consistency across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add necessary legal or contextual disclaimers (e.g., data limitations, jurisdictional notes) where applicable to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include EPA contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear EPA media contact details (name, phone, email) for follow-up questions from media and the public.
